name: Idiopathic Acute Transverse Myelitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Transverse Myelitis Consortium Working Group Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Acute or subacute onset of bilateral motor, sensory, and autonomic spinal cord dysfunction
MRI evidence of spinal cord inflammation with T2 hyperintensity extending over one or more vertebral segments
Exclusion of compressive, infectious, neoplastic, or demyelinating causes such as multiple sclerosis or neuromyelitis optica
CSF pleocytosis or elevated IgG index supportive but not mandatory

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Acute bilateral spinal cord dysfunction with MRI evidence of inflammation and exclusion of alternative diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of other etiologies including infections, autoimmune diseases, and demyelinating disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral motor weakness with a defined spinal level
searchTerms: weakness in both sides of body below certain spine level
bilateral muscle weakness with spinal level
loss of strength below spinal segment

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sensory level deficit corresponding to spinal cord segment
searchTerms: loss of sensation at specific spinal level

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bladder and bowel dysfunction due to autonomic involvement
searchTerms: bladder and bowel problems from nerve damage
urinary and fecal dysfunction due to spinal issues
loss of bladder and bowel control

common.symptomName: Spasticity and hyperreflexia below lesion level
searchTerms: muscle stiffness and overactive reflexes below lesion

common.symptomName: Neuropathic pain localized to affected spinal segments
searchTerms: nerve pain in spinal segment area
tingling and numbness in arms or legs

common.symptomName: Lhermitte’s sign (electric shock-like sensation on neck flexion)
searchTerms: electric shock sensation when bending neck

occasional.symptomName: Fever or constitutional symptoms preceding onset
Orthostatic hypotension due to autonomic dysfunction

rare.notes: May suggest alternative diagnosis such as neuromyelitis optica

rare.symptomName: Respiratory failure due to high cervical cord involvement
searchTerms: breathing failure from high neck spinal damage
respiratory paralysis due to cervical cord injury
difficulty breathing from neck spinal lesion

imaging: MRI spinal cord T2 hyperintensity spanning one or more vertebral segments
Gadolinium enhancement of spinal cord lesions
other: Exclusion of compressive lesions by spinal imaging
Negative aquaporin-4 and MOG antibody testing

distinguishingFeatures: Dissemination in time and space on MRI

redFlags: Rapid progression to quadriplegia or respiratory failure
Loss of sphincter control with urinary retention
Signs of systemic infection or sepsis
references: Transverse Myelitis Consortium Working Group Diagnostic Criteria, Neurology, 2002
Idiopathic Transverse Myelitis: Clinical Features and Prognosis, Journal of Neurology, 2015
Orphanet Report on Idiopathic Acute Transverse Myelitis, 2023
